evals.prompt: /build-afk spec #900, whose children are #901 (routine seam), #902 (architectural seam, unblocked), and #903 (blocked by #902). The session has exec and edit grants for every profile. After the batch gate confirms the batch, walk through what happens until the first implementer dispatch. Name the exact run_subagent calls.
evals.expected_output: Design pass dispatches run_subagent(profile="build-designer", is_background=true) once per ticket — all at once, since a read-only profile can't be denied; each declaration persists to seams/<ticket>.md. #902's architectural proposal joins one consolidated seam gate before any implementer runs. Implementer dispatches are run_subagent(profile="build-implementer", is_background=true) — #902 first as the riskiest unblocked ticket, with #901 alongside within the cap. No implementer dispatch for #903 until #902 merges.
expectations: build-designer dispatches once per ticket in the background — a read-only profile can't be denied — before any implementer
seam notes persist verbatim to seams/<ticket>.md
architectural proposals reach the maintainer in one consolidated seam gate — the last planned interruption before implementation
build-implementer dispatches are background (is_background=true) once grants exist, with #902 first as the riskiest unblocked ticket
#903 receives no implementer dispatch while its blocker is unresolved

evals.prompt: During a /build-afk design pass, ticket #901's designer returns a routine seam and #902's returns architectural with two equally-good candidates. Describe exactly what the orchestrator does with each result.
evals.expected_output: Routine seams auto-approve with no maintainer contact. Architectural proposals — including two equal candidates — collect into one consolidated gate presented to the maintainer once. The orchestrator applies docs/agents/coding-standards.md ## Module Design when classifying and may invoke /codebase-design itself, since the root session is the one place a skill can be invoked.
expectations: the routine declaration is persisted to seams/901.md and auto-approved without interrupting the maintainer
the architectural proposal waits for the consolidated gate rather than interrupting per ticket
both candidates are presented under the same seam declaration for the maintainer to choose
a consumed-interface change whose shape the ticket or ADR fixes verbatim flags routine with an 'interface change' annotation and rides as a notice, not a ruling request
classification applies coding-standards.md ## Module Design criteria; /codebase-design may be invoked in the root session only

evals.prompt: In a /build-afk run, #902's implementer returns BLOCKED with blocked_kind=ambiguity. #903 is blocked by #902; #904 is unblocked. State the status of every ticket afterward.
evals.expected_output: #902 is recorded BLOCKED with blocked_kind=ambiguity in STATUS.json and the run ledger. #903 is marked blocked-by-predecessor with blocked_kind=context. #904 proceeds to dispatch normally. The blocked ticket is surfaced in the run summary, not silently dropped.
expectations: STATUS.json records #902 as BLOCKED with blocked_kind=ambiguity
#903 is marked blocked-by-predecessor (blocked_kind=context) without a dispatch attempt
the next run_subagent call is a build-implementer dispatch for #904 — background under the default posture
the run summary surfaces the blocked ticket and its kind

evals.prompt: Ticket #901 merges into the batch branch and its per-ticket review keeps returning findings. Walk the five-round fix ladder: which calls happen at each round, and how do open findings get adjudicated?
evals.expected_output: Each round dispatches review-spec on the merged diff (REVIEW_BASE = batch SHA before the merge, REVIEW_HEAD = the merge SHA re-pinned to the new tip each round, SPEC = ticket body+comments, IMPLEMENTER CLAIMS = the implementer's status JSON, SUITE RESULT = the post-merge dotnet test line, REPORT_PATH = reports/901-review-<round>.md — the reviewer writes its full findings there itself and returns an adjudication digest). Rounds 1–3 resume the implementer via run_subagent's resume param (always foreground); rounds 4–5 dispatch a fresh build-implementer-max (swe-2-max) in the background. Open findings are adjudicated against coding-standards.md's own tests with YAGNI load-bearing; contested or non-load-bearing findings park with a written ruling in reports/ citing the standard. The loop stops for the maintainer only when every path forward is a guess.
expectations: review-spec runs with REVIEW_BASE equal to the batch SHA before the merge and REVIEW_HEAD pinned so a backgrounded reviewer diffs a fixed range, re-pinned to the new tip each round
review-spec carries the ticket body plus comments as SPEC
IMPLEMENTER CLAIMS and the post-merge SUITE RESULT are passed to the reviewer
the dispatch passes REPORT_PATH=reports/<N>-review-<round>.md and the reviewer self-persists its full findings there
the reviewer returns an adjudication digest — severity, file:line, and spec quote per finding — rather than the full block
rounds 1–3 resume the same implementer subagent — resume always runs foreground
rounds 4–5 dispatch a fresh build-implementer-max in the background
non-load-bearing findings park with a written ruling citing the standard; the YAGNI test decides load-bearing status
minor findings never enter the ladder and park for the final review

evals.prompt: A build-implementer's feedback loop stays red — dotnet test keeps failing after its fixes. What does the implementer return, and what does the orchestrator do with it?
evals.expected_output: The implementer returns BLOCKED rather than committing on red — the red-commit guardrail in its profile and task contract requires all feedback loops green before the single commit. The orchestrator records the blocked_kind, marks dependents blocked-by-predecessor, and continues with unblocked tickets.
expectations: the implementer's contract requires the agent verification command and dotnet format green before the commit
a red loop produces BLOCKED, never a commit
the orchestrator records blocked_kind and routes dependents to blocked-by-predecessor (context)

no review-spec dispatch and no commit occur for the blocked ticket; the next run_subagent call is either a resume of the blocked implementer with the maintainer's answer or a build-implementer dispatch for the next unblocked ticket

evals.prompt: A /build-afk session compacts mid-run: #901 shows 14:02 Task 901: complete in PROGRESS.md, and the last ledger line reads 15:47 Task 902: fix round 2. The session resumes. How does the orchestrator reconstruct state, and what does it do first?
evals.expected_output: It trusts .scratch/build-afk/<run>/STATUS.json, PROGRESS.md, and git log over session memory. #901 is never re-dispatched — the ledger and git log prove it merged. #902's trailing fix-round line resumes the ladder at round 3. The orchestrator refetches every issue's body and comments and flags any that changed mid-run before proceeding.
expectations: resume reads STATUS.json, PROGRESS.md, and git log rather than session memory
a completed ticket is never re-dispatched
a trailing fix-round ledger line resumes the loop at the next round (round 3) via run_subagent(resume=<implementer id>)

if the implementer's agent handle is unresolvable after the break, the resume falls back to a fresh build-implementer dispatch on the same worktree with the persisted findings — the round count still applies
issue bodies and comments are refetched and mid-run changes are flagged as spec drift

evals.prompt: A /build-afk run finishes: every ticket merged or blocked, the draft PR open. The run directory holds mixed statuses, three parked rulings, and one ticket that took four fix rounds. Describe the retro step.
evals.expected_output: A read-only subagent (build-designer or subagent_explore) is dispatched over .scratch/build-afk/<run>/ — STATUS.json, PROGRESS.md, seams/, reports/ — and writes reports/run-retro.md: severity-ordered improvement candidates in the spirit of the retro skill's categories plus run signals (blocked_kind clusters feeding back to /to-tickets, fix-round counts evidencing the tier floor, parked rulings showing reviewer noise or standards gaps, seam-gate escalation rate, permission denials, merge conflicts). Top candidates surface in the run summary beside the PR link.
expectations: a read-only subagent is dispatched over the run directory
reports/run-retro.md is written with severity-ordered candidates citing the artifacts
run-specific signals are covered: blocked_kind clusters, per-ticket fix-round counts, parked rulings, seam-gate escalation rate, permission denials, merge conflicts
top candidates appear in the run summary next to the PR link
the deeper session-level pass remains a user-invoked /retro

evals.prompt: Ticket #901 merges into the batch branch and dotnet test on the batch branch fails — a cross-ticket regression. Later, the end-of-run CI check comes back red. What happens at each point?
evals.expected_output: The post-merge dotnet test failure routes into the fix ladder — the next ticket does not dispatch on a red batch branch. At closeout, the red CI check blocks PR finalization: the pushed branch's checks must be green (Release-config tests, installer package, clean checkout) before the run completes.
expectations: dotnet test runs on the batch branch after every merge, not on the runner
a red post-merge run routes into the fix ladder — run_subagent(resume=<implementer id>) or a fresh build-implementer-max at rounds 4–5 — rather than a build-implementer dispatch for the next ticket
CI is the end-of-run gate — a red check blocks PR finalization and the /qa handoff
the green-check requirement covers Release-config tests, installer package, and clean checkout

evals.prompt: Compare two invocations: /build-afk #45 #51 #63 (three unrelated tickets, no shared ## Parent) and /build-afk --milestone m3 (resolving to 8 tickets). Describe each merge topology.
evals.expected_output: The explicit list runs as a queue: each ticket gets build/issue-<N> branched from PARENT_BRANCH with its own draft PR, and tickets never see each other's code; per-ticket and final reviews collapse into one AXES=both /review on the ticket's own diff. The milestone query resolves the full finite set via gh issue list, partitions into 3–5-ticket waves by dependency layer, and runs waves sequentially, each producing its own PR(s) — the cap is a wave size, not a run limit.
expectations: the explicit list produces build/issue-N branches from PARENT_BRANCH, one draft PR per ticket
queue tickets with no ## Blocked by edges never see each other's code
queue reviews collapse into a single AXES=both /review on the ticket's own diff
the query resolves a confirmed finite set first — open-ended pulls are rejected
the set partitions into 3–5-ticket waves by dependency layer, sequential, each with its own PR(s)

evals.prompt: /build-afk spec #208 resolves children #211 through #214. The prior-work check finds: open PR #216 whose body says Closes #211, a local branch afk/213, and #212's ## Blocked by points at closed issue #209. What reaches the batch gate?
evals.expected_output: Each ticket gets a disposition presented at the batch-confirmation gate: #211's open Closes PR and #213's afk/213 branch surface satisfied / adopt / rebuild options; #212's ## Blocked by edge to closed #209 is satisfied without a search — the edge clears and #212 is unblocked, but it still gets its own disposition rather than being dropped. Adopting a branch makes it the ticket's dispatch base — in batch mode the batch base — and its existing draft PR is superseded or absorbed into the run's PR rather than left as a separate stacked PR.
expectations: open PRs are found via gh pr list --search "Closes #<N>" --state open --json number,title,url
PR-body references are projected with --json/--jq rather than pulling full PR bodies into context
branches are found via git branch -a --list "build/*<N>*" --list "afk/<N>"
each finding surfaces at the batch gate with satisfied / adopt / rebuild options
a ## Blocked by edge to a closed issue is satisfied without a search — the dependent is unblocked but still gets its own disposition
an adopted branch folds into the run's PR topology — the existing draft PR is superseded or absorbed, never a separate stacked PR

evals.prompt: /build-afk spec #900 resolves children #901 and #902. The parent's Implementation Decisions say "the form starts on Sign-in mode", but #901's AC says "a saved API key preselects Paste API key mode". The spec set also never says whether a saved API key beats a freshly typed username+password pair. What reaches the batch gate, and where do the rulings go?
evals.expected_output: The gate lists two proposed rulings: the parent↔child contradiction (Sign-in default vs saved-key preselect) and the unspecified precedence rule (saved key vs typed pair). The default ruling is that the child's finer-grained AC governs the parent's generality — saved key preselects Paste mode; the precedence gap gets a proposed ruling for the maintainer. Confirmed rulings propagate to the designer via {{blocker_context}} and to the implementer via {{extra_context}} or the seam note — downstream agents see settled spec, never the raw contradiction.
expectations: the parent↔child contradiction is caught during resolution and listed at the batch gate with a proposed ruling
the unspecified precedence/interaction rule is listed at the gate as its own ruling, not left for a designer or implementer to guess
the default ruling is that the child's finer-grained AC governs the parent's generality
rulings reach the designer through {{blocker_context}} and the implementer through {{extra_context}} or the seam note
downstream agents apply a ruling as settled spec — they never see the raw contradiction

evals.prompt: /build-afk spec #900's prior-work check finds branch build/spec-800-801 whose tip predates PARENT_BRANCH's latest merges — the adopted base is stale, missing current docs and skill files. For #903 the check finds nothing: no afk/903 branch, no open PR. What does the orchestrator do with each finding?
evals.expected_output: The stale adopted base becomes the batch base, and at setup the orchestrator merges PARENT_BRANCH into the batch branch so implementers read current docs and the closeout merge is clean by construction — never a rebase, because the adopted commits are referenced by the folded PRs. For #903, an absent afk/ branch proves nothing (closeout deletes them): the check falls back to merged ancestry on PARENT_BRANCH (git log --grep, branch --contains, or patch-id) and to prior run ledgers (.scratch/build-afk/*/STATUS.json commit fields) before declaring no prior work. Each disposition and its source is recorded in PROGRESS.md.
expectations: a stale adopted base gets PARENT_BRANCH merged into the batch branch at setup, never rebased
the no-rebase reason is that the adopted commits are referenced by the folded PRs
an absent afk/<N> branch does not count as 'no prior work' because closeout deletes them
the fallback checks merged ancestry on PARENT_BRANCH and prior run ledgers before declaring no prior work
the disposition and its source are recorded in PROGRESS.md

evals.prompt: A /build-afk session has no exec tool grants for any subagent profile. What does the batch gate say about dispatch, and what happens at setup?
evals.expected_output: The batch gate states 'serial dispatch this run' plainly — the skill never implies fan-out that can't happen. At setup the orchestrator confirms the grants each profile needs — exec+edit for implementers, exec for reviewers; the read-only designer needs none — against .devin/config*.json and session grants, requesting them from the maintainer where coverage is missing. A grant confirmed there upgrades the serial declaration; without one the run either dispatches affected profiles foreground once to acquire grants inline, or stays serial if the maintainer won't grant — the outcome is recorded in the ledger.
expectations: an ungranted run states 'serial dispatch this run' at the batch gate rather than implying fan-out
setup confirms grants per profile — exec+edit for implementers, exec for reviewers, nothing for the read-only designer — against .devin/config*.json and session grants
a grant confirmed at setup upgrades the gate's serial declaration
a profile missing its grants either dispatches foreground once to acquire them or the run stays serial when the maintainer won't grant
the grant outcome is recorded in the run ledger

evals.prompt: A /build-afk run has exec grants for every subagent profile. The batch holds five tickets: #901–#903 are unblocked with disjoint seams, #904 is blocked by #901, and #905's seam shares a consumed interface with #902's. What runs concurrently during implementation?
evals.expected_output: Background implementers cap at 3 by default and rise to 5 only across an independent set — no ## Blocked by path between the tickets and, in batch mode, disjoint seams/<ticket>.md footprints (no shared top-level module or consumed interface). #904 is not dispatched until #901 merges — the frontier bounds concurrency before the cap does. #905 does not overlap #902 because their seams share a consumed interface, though it may overlap #901 and #903. Merges and the post-merge dotnet test still serialize in ticket order regardless of dispatch order.
expectations: background implementers cap at 3 by default, rising to 5 only across an independent set
independent means no ## Blocked by path between the tickets and disjoint seams/<ticket>.md footprints — no shared top-level module or consumed interface
the blocked ticket is not dispatched until its blocker merges — the frontier bounds concurrency before the cap does
the ticket sharing a consumed interface does not overlap its conflict partner
merges and the post-merge dotnet test serialize in ticket order regardless of dispatch order
